envelope.description: Add the section-anchor model and the pure index deriver

body.title: Add the section-anchor model and the pure index deriver
body.summary: Add the sc3 declarations — SectionAnchor, SectionIndex, SectionResolver — plus the pure host-side deriveSectionIndex that backs them, with full unit coverage. All four names return zero source matches today, so this is net-new code that shadows nothing. Pure by construction: no DOM, no vscode import, no IO, so it is unit-testable headlessly and importable by s3 and s4. Deliberately INERT — nothing consumes it until t4 — which is why it lands before the render change rather than alongside it. REVISED per critique: dependsOn is now empty, because this module touches no file t1 or t2 touches; only its order (before t4) is a real constraint, so the build is free to take it first.
acceptanceChecks: deriveSectionIndex returns anchors in document order with level set to the ATX depth
two identically-titled headings receive DISTINCT slugs via an appended ordinal and neither entry is dropped
a `#`-prefixed line inside a fenced code block is NOT treated as a heading — the phantom-section guard
markdown with no headings, and an empty-string body, both yield an empty anchors array
a heading whose text is entirely punctuation still yields a stable NON-EMPTY slug
deriveSectionIndex is deterministic — the same markdown yields identical slugs across repeated calls
a SectionResolver resolves a known ofSectionId to that section's slug and returns undefined (never throws) for an unknown one
the slug deriveSectionIndex emits for a heading is the SAME string the resolver returns for it — asserted directly
the module declaring these remains vscode-free and imports no DOM type
